name: Both-Sides Dismantlability Preserves a coDamp Product
statement: If $C\in\mathsf{coDamp}$ and $D\in\mathcal B$ use disjoint coordinates, then $C\times D\in\mathsf{coDamp}$.
proof: Writing $P=C^c$ and $Q=D^c$, the product complement is $(P\times\{0,1\}^Y)\cup(\{0,1\}^X\times Q)$. Follow a corner deletion of $P$ one row at a time; within the row of its next corner, use the relative deletion from the full $Y$-cube down to $Q$ supplied by the dismantling of $D$. Each deleted vertex has the product of its two corner cubes present. The terminal class is the dismantlable product of a full cube with $Q$.
comments: This does not prove that the entire dismantlable-complement class is product closed; the second factor must itself and its complement be dismantlable.
